I am 65 this year, started farming when I was 15, only got a few years of primary school. My farm is 10.1 mu in Quzhou County, just me and my wife. We have a well that pumps good water. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone here.

For winter wheat, I plant in early October. I use improved seed, the kind the dealer sells—Jimai or something like that—about 30 jin per mu. For base fertilizer I put down one full 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, so that is 7.5 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium right there. When the wheat turns green in March, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 25 kg, which gives another 11.5 kg nitrogen. I know fertilizer got more expensive this year, but I do not dare cut back. A bad harvest means disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just money down the drain. I water wheat three times: before winter freeze, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. I spray twice—once for weeds in spring, once for insects or disease if they show up. Before planting wheat I plough deep to bury the maize stalks.

After harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize right away. I use about 3 kg of hybrid seed per mu. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the row at planting, which is 6 kg each of N, P, and K. At big trumpet stage I side-dress 20 kg of urea per mu, about 9 kg more nitrogen. Maize gets two irrigations: one if sowing is dry, and one at silking. Two sprays—herbicide first, then insecticide if the worms come. After wheat harvest I only have a few days, so I rotary till fast and get the seed in the ground. During harvest and planting I hire two people for 3-4 days, 150 yuan a day plus lunch.

I watch what my neighbors do. Old Wang and Li use about the same fertilizer. If everyone puts a bag and a half, I put a bag and a half. I learned this from my father and from watching others. That is my plan for this year.
